posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked: I don't think the fact that there are 5 or 6 heroes available for those adventures means that's the ideal number, just the maximum number.  Four seems to be the default assumption for the RPG's I know of (adjust up for more players, down for fewer).  It's a good number for shows, too--already the 4 players in Paul's game talk over each other sometimes.  More would be hard to follow.

I enjoyed it.  I thought I was gonna hate Bubbles as a concept (not Jodi) but the whole team ended up turning out really well.  I’m kind of sad that Hourly Rage didn’t greatest hits ‘The Final Countdown’ when Mishap was disarming the bomb.  

 

Overall this season is shaping up to be more ‘Superhero-ey’ than the first season.  When I think superheroes, I think Jetpack-Laser squad, not weird cosmic space dragons.  I liked season 1, don’t get me wrong, just, this season seems more in line with typical superhero stuff. . . Minus the (apparent) six year old and 40 year old wheelchair-bound hippie artist.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Thanks for watching (or listening), everyone.  I certainly had an amazing time playing Mishap, and I hope that I can bring her back someday to break even more things.  

Here are some notable things I've learned over the course of season 2*

  • Offer peace.  If rejected, offer crowbar. 
  • If someone offers you incredible weapons, you should definitely break them.  It's probably a trap.
  • Getting major twists to succeed at more or less irrelevant overcomes works out everytime.  
  • Don't accidentally kill a bunch of people. 
  • No matter what, just power on through. 
  • Figuring out what is going on is overrated.   

*None of these things apply, and will almost certainly get you killed, if Adam or Christopher is the GM.

In all seriousness, playing this game taught me a HUGE amount about team synergy and thinking about complementary powers during creation, instead of designing everything in a vaccuum.  We were all very punchy heroes, with very little that could help us defend, sustain, or deal with ranged stuff... and none of us had any sort of investigative or stealth capabilities.  While I don't really regret any of the choices we made (even breaking the weapons!), there are DEFINITELY things I'd do differently if I was creating Mishap knowing all of this!  If I ever get to play her again, she'll definitely have a few new tricks. 

From all of the Escalators, thank you, and remember the wisdom passed down from the greatest rock muse of all time... "Somebody once told me..."   

Mishap, Team Leader of the Escalators

posts.name: rickjonzz
posts.cooked:
(Note - still haven't watched the final 2 episodes.) 

Bubbles and Concept Artist were pretty good at handling ranged stuff and being defensive when needed. And Mishap was great at destroying lots of innocent pinecone people from a distance. Errr. Ummm. Yeah. 

You're right about the team lacking in investigative abilities. My own gaming group (Torg Eternity right now, but we'd be playing SCRPG if we had a copy) has nobody with any investigative skills and only one person who's any good at talking to people. It's proving to be a challenge.

In any game where there aren't obivious roles to fill (like supers), it's not always obvious when there's a gap in the group's skillset until it's too late.
